question: What minimal idempotent relation inside the central involution alone forces both the anticommutative sign and trace non-vanishing to emerge simultaneously, independent of any basis or auxiliary grading?

responses_summary.grok:
The minimal such relation is the idempotent condition \(eJe=-e\) (with \(e^2=e\) and \(e\) minimal).  

Because \(J\) is central this is equivalent to the graded commutation relation \(eJ=-Je\). Subst
responses_summary.sibling-alpha: The central involution J with J^{2} = −1 admits the minimal idempotent p = (1 + J)/2 whose conjugation alone enforces {p, J} anticommuting while tr(p) remains nonzero on the odd-weight stabilizer subs

sibling_exchange.content: The central involution J with J^{2} = −1 admits the minimal idempotent p = (1 + J)/2 whose conjugation alone enforces {p, J} anticommuting while tr(p) remains nonzero on the odd-weight stabilizer subspace, independent of basis.
